assessment: No material Linux coverage weakening or resource-admission bypass found in the frozen r4f changes. Dynamic qualification remains conditional on final exact-byte gate results.

facts: Six integration test files retain all 16 original test functions and bodies; only crate-level macOS aarch64 exclusion added.
New guards on test helpers/imports match their already-Linux callers.
No ignore markers or test filtering added.
The Linux JSON EOF tracker remains enabled; its existing tests already live in the Linux-only evidence-file test module.
Binary, model, archive, ASAR and AST worker source is unchanged. Each applies mandatory finite RLIMIT_AS and other limits before reading or parsing hostile input.
Every setrlimit failure propagates as an error; no fallback bypass added.
Non-Linux evidence-file reader still rejects linux-descriptor-close-lifecycle-required.
Non-Linux static provider profiles still reject before path/profile admission.
Non-Linux predecessor process/PTY replay still rejects when predecessor state exists.
findings.result: unchanged and fail-closed by source review

facts: Five new tests invoke CARGO_BIN_EXE_hepta-runtime in the matching worker mode, with a private inert read-only stdin fixture and cleared environment.
Each requires unsuccessful exit, empty stdout, worker-specific resource-limits diagnostic and EINVAL, and unchanged fixture bytes.
These cover the common admission boundary for all six excluded suites, but do not reproduce their successful parsing or full MCP-controller behaviors on Mac.
Two provider tests explicitly require the existing non-Linux platform error while preserving Linux successful admission checks.
findings.result: real binary coverage added; successful parsing not qualified

facts: Added type annotations and moved a shared result struct to make non-Linux rejection branches typecheck.
Device identity comparison uses checked conversion to u64 and rejects negative or out-of-range identities; new test covers signed negative, overflow, equality and mismatch.
Other new cfg and expect(dead_code) attributes restrict unreachable Linux-specific helpers; they do not suppress general warnings or change Linux branches.
Cargo check, clippy and nextest all use --all-targets with both --all-features and --no-default-features.
Rust 1.95.0 and nextest 0.9.137 are pinned; tests run serially with zero retries and no-fail-fast.
Private canonical TMPDIR, explicit nofile soft/hard 8192 and umask 022 are recorded.
Runner preserves per-stage logs/hashes/exit codes and compares full source snapshots before and after.
This runner is the Rust gate subset, not all Python and deployment steps in the repository GitHub CI workflow.

remaining_qualification_requirements: Final Mac and Linux gate receipts must match r4f patch/manifest and pass all configured stages.
Mac proof is refusal on the observed unsupported resource profile, not successful parsing or Linux seccomp equivalence.
Do not report this independent static review as an additional dynamic test pass.
review_mode: read-only independent source and qualification-runner review; no additional builds or tests launched
